original_question: Find the asymptotic value of phi(n,4,5), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set in which every four-point subset determines at least five distinct distances.
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 31 of the current arXiv version: the open problem asking for the asymptotic value of φ(n,4,5). In the June 7, 2014 PDF draft of the same survey, this is the corresponding Section 6, Problem 30.
correct_elements: Your draft already names the correct quantity φ(n,4,5), places the problem in the plane, states the right local hypothesis on every 4-point subset, and asks for the asymptotic value. That matches the paper’s official open problem essentially verbatim.
missing_details: State the formal definition of φ(n,4,5) as a minimum over all finite sets P ⊂ R^2 with |P| = n.
Specify that distances are Euclidean distances in R^2, counted by distinct numerical values among unordered pairs of points.
Make the local condition fully explicit: for every subset Q ⊂ P with |Q| = 4, the six pairwise distances determined by Q contain at least 5 distinct values.
State that the asymptotic question is as n → ∞ through positive integers.
Make clear that no additional assumptions such as general position, non-collinearity, or non-cocircularity are imposed beyond the 4-point local distance condition.
To reflect the nearby context in the paper, note that Erdős specifically asked whether φ(n,4,5) has quadratic order, i.e. φ(n,4,5) = Θ(n^2).

Do not recast the question as a forbidden-quadrilateral classification problem: unlike the φ(n,4,3) and φ(n,4,4) cases, the paper does not give an explicit equivalent forbidden-pattern reformulation for φ(n,4,5).
refined_question: For each positive integer n, let φ(n,4,5) be the minimum possible value of D(P), where P ⊂ R^2 is an n-point set and D(P) denotes the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by unordered pairs of points of P, under the condition that every 4-point subset Q ⊂ P determines at least 5 distinct distances among its 6 pairwise distances. Determine the asymptotic growth of φ(n,4,5) as n → ∞. In particular, is Erdős’s suggested quadratic behavior φ(n,4,5) = Θ(n^2) correct?
justification: The draft is already aimed at the exact official problem in the paper. Section 7 introduces φ(n,k,l) as the minimum number of distinct distances in an n-point planar set for which every k-point subset determines at least l distinct distances. In the k = 4 discussion, the paper isolates the φ(n,4,5) case, notes that Erdős asked whether it should be quadratic, records only the trivial Ω(n) lower bound, and then states the open problem as “Find the asymptotic value of φ(n,4,5).” So the right refinement is not a broader local-properties question, not the neighboring φ(n,4,4) or φ(n,5,9) problems, and not a forbidden-configuration reformulation. The only needed sharpening is to spell out the Euclidean ambient space, the precise minimization, the quantifier over all 4-subsets, and that the asymptotic is taken as n grows.
